runTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) of an episode (not necessarily DONE).

savePrompt.description: If true, the LLM prompt produced by the harness is included as a 'prompt' field on the action returned by core_harness, which causes it to be persisted in the episode replay. Defaults to false to keep replays small.

seed.description: Integer currently only used for selecting starting position.

strictMode.description: If true, agents must return only {'submission': int} (no extra fields like 'thoughts'), and per-agent TIMEOUT/ERROR/INVALID counts as a loss for the offending agent only — other agents win. If false (default), any agent error halts and voids the entire episode, matching the lenient research-mode behavior.

useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

useOpenings.description: Whether to start from a position in an opening book.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

action.thoughts:
The current board state is almost entirely empty, with the only pieces being an x (my piece) at row 0/column 3 and an o (opponent) directly above it at row 1/column 3. This means my first move (in column 3) has already been made, the opponent responded in the same column, and it is now my turn again.

No immediate threats or wins exist for either player (far too early in the game). Optimal strategy in Connect 4 prioritizes controlling the central columns (2-4), building connectivity for future horizontal/diagonal lines, and placing pieces at the lowest possible rows where possible.

Placing in column 3 now would drop an x at row 2/column 3. This creates no vertical connection to my existing bottom x (due to the blocking o) and does little to advance horizontal or diagonal threats. It is suboptimal.

Instead, the strongest move is to drop in an adjacent central column at the bottom row. This creates two adjacent x pieces along row 0 (a strong base for a horizontal 4-in-a-row) while also opening strong diagonal potential (e.g., via follow-up moves in the same column). Column 2 and column 4 are symmetric and equally strong here; column 2 is selected.

This leaves all other columns (0, 1, 5, 6) as inferior because they are too far from the center and do not connect to my existing piece.

Final Answer: 2

action.thoughts:
The current board has only four pieces placed: X in row 5, columns 2 and 3 (bottom row), and O in column 3 at rows 3 and 4. No player has a completed line of 4, and neither can win on the immediate next turn (O has only two pieces total).

Playing in column 1 drops an X to row 5, column 1. This creates three consecutive X pieces along the bottom row (columns 1-2-3). This sets up an immediate fork: on the following turn, I can complete four-in-a-row horizontally by dropping in either column 0 (columns 0-1-2-3) or column 4 (columns 1-2-3-4). O can block at most one of those two columns on their intervening turn, so the win is forced on my next move regardless of O's response.

(The symmetric move in column 4 creates an equivalent fork with three X on the bottom in columns 2-3-4 and open wins in columns 1 or 5.) No other move creates a faster or more forcing win, and there is no need to block O yet (O cannot reach four-in-a-row before I win).

Final Answer: 1
